origin.description: Writes the 1-based index of the polygon with the greatest coverage. A tie keeps the lower index.
origin.details: Writes the 1-based index of the polygon with the greatest coverage. A tie keeps the lower index.
origin.value: A raster, a number, or a matrix of polygon indexes.
origin.example:
g <- sf::st_sf(geometry=sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(c(0,0, 2,0, 2,2, 0,2, 0,0), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE))),
  sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(c(1,1, 3,1, 3,3, 1,3, 1,1), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)))
))
y <- raster::raster(xmn=0, xmx=3, ymn=0, ymx=3, nrows=3, ncols=3)
m <- as.matrix(rasterize_polygons(g, y))
writeLines(apply(m, 1, function(row) paste(ifelse(is.na(row), "NA", as.character(row)), collapse=" ")))

translation.description: Writes the 1-based index of the polygon with the greatest coverage. A tie keeps the lower index.
translation.details: Writes the 1-based index of the polygon with the greatest coverage. A tie keeps the lower index. A grid is an extent and a resolution, with values when the cells hold data. A polygon is WKT. Row 0 is north.
translation.value: A dict with values and an extent, a list of those, or a list of numbers.
